claims.text: W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf is proposed as a Group IV-V refractory high-entropy alloy system.
The initial powder blend consists of W, Ta, Hf, V, and Nb with controlled O and N impurity levels.
The proposed alloy is intended to form a single-phase BCC solid solution upon rapid solidification.
Low laser scan speed and small hatch distance produce lower growth rate and higher temperature gradient, promoting cellular rather than dendritic solidification.
Rapid SLM solidification refines grains and reduces dendrite or cellular arm spacing.
Cold rolling followed by annealing at 900 °C and aging at 650 °C can generate a homogeneous intragranular precipitate distribution.
The post-processing route will generate coherent δ-lamellae or γ″ nanoprecipitates within the proposed BCC matrix.
Homogeneous intragranular precipitation rather than grain-boundary precipitation reduces intergranular embrittlement.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations.
Coherent precipitates prevent premature crack initiation while retaining ductility.
The proposed cellular and coherent-precipitate microstructure will mitigate brittleness caused specifically by O and N segregation.
Use of a room-temperature SLM build platform can be compatible with brittleness mitigation in the proposed alloy.
The optimized alloy will attain microhardness above 600 HV.
The optimized alloy will exhibit tensile elongation above 10%.
The optimized alloy will retain structural integrity at temperatures up to 800 °C.
The optimized alloy will avoid brittle TCP phases and intergranular cracks.
Conventionally cast refractory HEAs can have grain sizes near 200 μm and dendrite arm spacings of 20–30 μm.
Refractory HEAs can crack because process-induced internal stress acts together with low-temperature ductility and brittle impurity-bearing grain boundaries.
Above an unspecified interstitial-impurity threshold, O or N will segregate to boundaries faster than the treatment can homogenize the alloy.

contradictions.description: The target composition is not internally fixed: the hypothesis and experiment specify W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf, whereas the initial powder state specifies W-Ta-Hf-V-Nb, adding Nb and omitting Cr.

The conditions suggest a room-temperature build platform as part of brittleness mitigation, while the uncertainty states that mitigation without a high-temperature build platform has not been demonstrated; the cited room-temperature PBF-LB/M evidence instead reports cracking.
